newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies close sharply higher.

text.p: CME pork belly futures rallied sharply to close higher, rising from early profit-taking losses on renewed demand amid strong cash product prices and on firm technical factors, traders said.
February ran up to 78.675 cents, its highest level since October 10, before closing at 78.575, up 1.775 cent. Other months finished 1.600 to 1.375 cents higher.
The reduced pace of hog slaughter, firm cash belly market and strong technical picture combined to boost prices.
"Bacon sales are strong at both retail and (fast food) outlets," one trader said.

Continued private reports of $70 per cwt being paid for next week delivery on cash bellies and retailer featuring of bacon made the premium of futures over cash look much too narrow and futures rallied from early profit taking. USDA reported Thursday sales at $68, the highest price level since early October.
Technicals also pointed higher after futures reached one-month highs.
"The charts show 'up' and that's where we are headed," one chartist in the belly pit said.
Dean Witter and Cargill Investor Services bought February at the close with Prudential Securities a notable buyer during the day, pit sources said.
In belly options, Lind-Waldock sold February 84 calls. Volatility was up, pit sources added.
Profit taking continued in hog futures, especially after the runup to a new contract high in December and continued talk of packers cutting slaughter plans, traders said.
Hogs closed 0.050 to 0.225 cent lower with December off 0.175 at 58.650 cents.
"Packers are going to cut kills and try to lower their bids (for cash hogs) next week," said Karl Skold, Director of Research for Frontier Risk Management.

December posted a new contract high on Thursday and closed limit up, but traded lower much of the day despite underlying support from longs who looked for continued support from light hog marketings. Marketings have been running under earlier projections and the trend is likely to continue as producers hold breeding stock amid reduced feed costs, they said.
Traders bullish the market noted that many packers were cutting back on kill rates due to a lack of available slaughter numbers and not because concerns over margins.
Cash hogs will likely be steady to firm Monday even with much better shipping weather, they said.

Rand Financials bought late after selling early. Refco also bought and locals covered short positions. Cargill Investor Services spread long February/short April. In hog options, trading was light with late scattered buying of December 58 puts. Volatility was unchanged, pit sources said.
